<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="סיון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918788_theRebbe_204" batchId="meluket-_D7_A1_D7_99_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918788_theRebbe_204__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the difference between "rain" and "dew" in the verse, relating rain to divine flow drawn through human effort (arousal from below) and dew to a spontaneous flow from above without any arousal from below.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, it was brought above,</t>
    <t s="2">that in the Gemara the verse was brought regarding this</t>
    <t s="3">(that Dovid said)</t>
    <t s="4">“A rain of freewill gifts You will pour forth, O G-d,” etc.,</t>
    <t s="5">and at first glance it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="6">behold in the verse it is written “rain of freewill gifts,”</t>
    <t s="7">specifically rain,</t>
    <t s="8">and if so, what is it that it concludes that He returned to them with dew, may it be life,</t>
    <t s="9">specifically dew.</t>
    <t s="10">And it is explained in another place,</t>
    <t s="11">that the quality of “rain of freewill gifts”</t>
    <t s="12">(not ordinary rain)</t>
    <t s="13">is similar to the matter of dew.</t>
    <t s="14">But still it needs to be understood why it is specifically called by the name “rain.”</t>
    <t s="15">And the explanation of the matter will be understood based on what is explained by the Mitteler Rebbe in his maamar beginning with “Inyan Tal Torah,”</t>
    <t s="16">(and it is a continuation of the discourse beginning “To understand the matter of the Omer of barley and the two loaves” that was stated above in this discourse of the Rebbe the Tzemach Tzedek),</t>
    <t s="17">for it is written,</t>
    <t s="18">“May my teaching drop as the rain, my speech flow as the dew,”</t>
    <t s="19">(for this is written regarding the Torah,</t>
    <t s="20">since Moshe Rabbeinu said,</t>
    <t s="21">“Moshe received the Torah from Sinai and transmitted it,” etc.,</t>
    <t s="22">to the extent that the Torah is called by his name),</t>
    <t s="23">behold there are in the Torah two levels: the aspect of dew and the aspect of rain.</t>
    <t s="24">And he explains regarding this,</t>
    <t s="25">for it is known that rain comes about because of vapors that rise from the earth, etc.</t>
    <t s="26">[And as it is written,</t>
    <t s="27">“And a mist ascended from the earth and watered the entire face of the ground,”</t>
    <t s="28">this being the rain that waters the face of the earth,</t>
    <t s="29">and as it is written,</t>
    <t s="30">“For as the rain comes down, etc., waters the earth and causes it to bring forth and sprout, etc.”],</t>
    <t s="31">but the dew is that which descends from above by itself, as the statement,</t>
    <t s="32">“Dew is not withheld.”</t>
    <t s="33">And correspondingly, there are two kinds of drawings and influences from above,</t>
    <t s="34">one drawn from above downward through arousal from below,</t>
    <t s="35">this being the aspect of rain,</t>
    <t s="36">like the rain drawn by the vapor ascending from the earth,</t>
    <t s="37">meaning through toil and work from below.</t>
    <t s="38">And as our sages, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="39">on the verse “May my teaching drop as the rain,”</t>
    <t s="40">“When the creatures break their neck, immediately rain descends.”</t>
    <t s="41">And in the service of man, the aspect of “neck” is the aspect of the back</t>
    <t s="42">(the opposite of the aspect of the face),</t>
    <t s="43">“After the L-rd you shall go,”</t>
    <t s="44">and “the creatures break their neck” is the nullification of this matter</t>
    <t s="45">(of concealment and hiding)</t>
    <t s="46">that comes through work and toil.</t>
    <t s="47">And the intention in this is not the breaking of the body literally, heaven forbid,</t>
    <t s="48">but rather the soul is in the body,</t>
    <t s="49">a healthy body with all its 248 limbs and 365 sinews,</t>
    <t s="50">and the breaking is only the breaking of the heart alone</t>
    <t s="51">(and the breaking of the neck,</t>
    <t s="52">“What difference is there between killing the whole and killing half?”).</t>
    <t s="53">And on the contrary,</t>
    <t s="54">through the breaking of the heart the body comes to greater perfection,</t>
    <t s="55">as the well-known saying, “There is nothing as whole as a broken heart.”</t>
    <t s="56">And through this the rain descends from above,</t>
    <t s="57">and the rain waters the earth and causes it to bring forth and sprout, etc.</t>
    <t s="58">And the second drawing from above is the aspect of dew, which is drawn by itself without any arousal from below at all, like the dew that descends by itself,</t>
    <t s="59">as the statement, “Dew is not withheld”</t>
    <t s="60">(as above).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the two aspects of rain and dew in Torah correspond to the external (revealed) part of Torah drawn through human effort, and the inner (mystical) part of Torah that flows spontaneously, which will be fully revealed in the future.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is “May my teaching drop as the rain, my speech flow as the dew,”</t>
    <t s="2">for just as there are these two aspects</t>
    <t s="3">(arousal from above drawn through arousal from below, and arousal from above that is above arousal from below)</t>
    <t s="4">in the divine influences in general,</t>
    <t s="5">so too there are these two matters in the Torah</t>
    <t s="6">(“my teaching” and “my speech”).</t>
    <t s="7">For the matter of the flow of the light of Torah called “rain” is the aspect of the externality of Torah</t>
    <t s="8">(the revealed part of Torah)</t>
    <t s="9">drawn through man’s service and man’s toil.</t>
    <t s="10">And as the statement,</t>
    <t s="11">“I toiled and I found—believe,”</t>
    <t s="12">from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="13">that the finding is measured according to the value of the toil.</t>
    <t s="14">And although it is explained elsewhere,</t>
    <t s="15">that the matter of “finding” is not commensurate with the toil</t>
    <t s="16">(like a simple find, where the one who finds it does not know from whom the find came to him,</t>
    <t s="17">and he finds it incidentally),</t>
    <t s="18">nevertheless, it has some value and connection to the toil,</t>
    <t s="19">for if one toils in a place where the find is not, he will not find it,</t>
    <t s="20">and as it is written,</t>
    <t s="21">“And you shall seek from there, etc.,”</t>
    <t s="22">and it is explained in Likkutei Torah</t>
    <t s="23">that what it says “from there” specifically is because it is impossible to find a lost object except in the place where it was lost.</t>
    <t s="24">But the dew of Torah is the aspect of an influence that is drawn by itself,</t>
    <t s="25">and it is the aspect of “the dew of the pearls,”</t>
    <t s="26">“the dew that drips from the Ancient Holy One,”</t>
    <t s="27">with which He will in the future revive the dead,</t>
    <t s="28">the aspect of the innerness of Torah.</t>
    <t s="29">And therefore it is said of it “my speech flow as the dew,”</t>
    <t s="30">for the matter of “flow” is from the term “liquid,”</t>
    <t s="31">meaning that it is drawn and descends downward, downward as it is in its source and root in the aspect of the mazal.</t>
    <t s="32">And the revelation of the aspect of the dew of Torah will be in the future,</t>
    <t s="33">as explained in the continuation of the discourse there, that this is what our sages, of blessed memory, said, “Whoever engages in Torah, the dew of Torah revives him,”</t>
    <t s="34">that through engagement in the revealed part of Torah in this time, the aspect of the dew of Torah will be drawn in the future,</t>
    <t s="35">the innerness of Torah.</t>
    <t s="36">[And as also explained elsewhere</t>
    <t s="37">regarding what our sages, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="38">“Fortunate is he who comes here with his learning in his hand,”</t>
    <t s="39">that through study of the revealed part of Torah</t>
    <t s="40">(“his learning”)</t>
    <t s="41">in this time, one merits the revelation of the secrets of Torah in the future.]</t>
    <t s="42">And this is also what is written,</t>
    <t s="43">“A new Torah will go forth from Me.”</t>
    <t s="44">That the revelation of the aspect of the new Torah</t>
    <t s="45">(the dew of Torah)</t>
    <t s="46">will be specifically in the future.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the dew that revives the dead corresponds to the aspect of arousal from above that is beyond any arousal from below, which is why all Israel have a share in the resurrection, unlike the World to Come which depends on service.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And with this will also be understood that this aspect of dew is the dew with which He will in the future revive the dead,</t>
    <t s="2">for the innovation of the resurrection of the dead is that it is drawn from the aspect of arousal from above that is above arousal from below.</t>
    <t s="3">And as explained in several discourses</t>
    <t s="4">the innovation and change of the resurrection of the dead relative to the Garden of Eden.</t>
    <t s="5">For the resurrection of the dead is higher than the Garden of Eden,</t>
    <t s="6">as is proven from the wording of the blessing of Yotzer</t>
    <t s="7">(of Shabbos)</t>
    <t s="8">“There is no comparison, etc., and there is none besides You, our King, for the life of the World to Come”</t>
    <t s="9">(the Garden of Eden)</t>
    <t s="10">etc.</t>
    <t s="11">(and afterwards)</t>
    <t s="12">“And there is none like You, our Redeemer, for the resurrection of the dead,”</t>
    <t s="13">and nevertheless, regarding the Garden of Eden, man’s service is required,</t>
    <t s="14">both the service before this</t>
    <t s="15">(as preparation for the Garden of Eden)</t>
    <t s="16">and the service in the Garden of Eden itself,</t>
    <t s="17">this being the matter of the ascents in the Garden of Eden from level to level through the pillar that is between one Garden of Eden and another, etc.,</t>
    <t s="18">and not only this,</t>
    <t s="19">but not every person merits the Garden of Eden</t>
    <t s="20">(as the language is brought in many places)</t>
    <t s="21">(the upper one)</t>
    <t s="22">because it depends on service,</t>
    <t s="23">but regarding the resurrection of the dead we learned,</t>
    <t s="24">“All Israel have a share in the World to Come,”</t>
    <t s="25">and although it states in the continuation of the Mishnah “except for, etc.,”</t>
    <t s="26">nevertheless, it is explained in the Yerushalmi,</t>
    <t s="27">that through the clarification and refinement afterwards, they too will return to life.</t>
    <t s="28">And the reason for this is explained,</t>
    <t s="29">because the revelation of G-dliness in the Garden of Eden has its root in the aspect of arousal from above that is drawn through arousal from below,</t>
    <t s="30">from the aspect of that which fills all worlds,</t>
    <t s="31">and therefore it depends on man’s service,</t>
    <t s="32">but the revelation of the resurrection of the dead is from that which transcends all worlds,</t>
    <t s="33">arousal from above that is above arousal from below,</t>
    <t s="34">and therefore it does not depend on man’s service, but rather all Israel have a share in the World to Come.</t>
    <t s="35">And this is the matter of the dew of life,</t>
    <t s="36">as explained above,</t>
    <t s="37">that the aspect of dew is the aspect that is drawn by itself without any arousal from below.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
